correctness.rationale: For every finite interior block, an empty interval forces a sum of squared Gaussian displacements of \(N^3/12+O(N^2)\). The Gaussian covariance matrix has eigenvalues bounded by the exact AR(1) long-run variance, so a determinant moment bound yields the corresponding sharp one-sided cubic exponent. A finite Gaussian Markov block around a two-sided evacuation profile has density cost exactly \((1-\rho)^2N^3/[24\sigma^2(1-\rho^2)]+O(N^2)\). Its jump correction is \(O(N^2)\) by an exact summation-by-parts identity; the exterior Gaussian conditional tails are o(1) uniformly, making the lower bound genuine for the entire infinite point field. Integer-to-real monotonicity closes the quantifiers. The 15,353 exact-rational finite checks verify key algebraic identities but are not treated as asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact infinite-size logarithmic law for a natural correlated stationary point process rather than a restatement of general mixing bounds. The nontrivial change in the leading cubic cost with positive correlation, specifically the reciprocal long-run-variance law, gives a sharp geometric rarity invariant for the entire fixed-parameter AR(1) Gaussian family. It resolves a concrete precision gap left by the motivating treatment: upper bounds of stretched-exponential form and order-only Gaussian examples do not identify this coefficient.
